paper_id: Dong et al. - 2014 - Link Quality Aware Code Dissemination in Wireless Sensor Networks
title: Link Quality Aware Code Dissemination in Wireless Sensor Networks
venue: IEEE Transactions on Parallel and Distributed Systems
motivation: Wireless reprogramming is essential when physically collecting deployed sensor nodes is infeasible; GreenOrbs deployment required 127 software upgrades
problem_framing: Existing protocols suffer from low channel efficiency (14.3% for CC2420 with small packets) and suboptimal sender selection that ignores link quality
key_insight: Weight senders by uncovered neighbors multiplied by outbound link quality; larger packets improve efficiency but require link-aware sender selection to avoid losses
method_signature: ECD uses configurable packet sizes, link-quality-weighted impact estimation, and impact-based backoff timers for fast implicit coordination
evaluation_criteria: Completion time and data traffic volume compared against Deluge and MNP on 25-node testbed and TOSSIM simulations
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Large packets (92-byte payload) suffer performance degradation due to wireless loss susceptibility; sender selection cannot prevent hidden-terminal collisions
evidence_for_taste: put less weight on nodes with poor outbound link qualities
largest impact sender is most likely to transmit
largest packets does not lead to best performance
thinking_moves: 从部署现场痛点(版本升级需求)抽象出协议效率瓶颈
用具体数值(e.g., 14.3%效率)量化隐性问题
用拓扑示例(80 vs 50 transmissions)展示机制威力
承认大包策略有副作用,需配合sender selection
将MNP的显式多轮协调替换为隐式backoff机制
cites_own_work: Dong et al. - Bulk Data Dissemination (2009)
